items.title: Raxio builds Mozambique’s digital infrastructure ecosystem
items.summary: When we spoke in 2024, you expected data localisation, the financial sector and LNG to drive demand. Two years on, has that translated into real business? Many of the market developments we anticipated are now becoming visible. Financial institutions and connectivity providers were important drivers of our initial demand, and we are also seeing growing participation from cloud and digital-service providers as the local ecosystem develops A particularly important development has been the evolution of Mozambique’s regulatory framework. The country has introduced regulations covering data centres and cloud computing and has continued to strengthen its broader cybersecurity, cybercrime and data-protection environment This creates greater clarity around how critical digital infrastructure should be operated and how sensitive and essential services should be supported.

items.title: Government to boost public investment budget by 3.6 billion meticais
items.summary: Maputo, 26 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican government intends to increase the public investment budget by 3.6 billion meticais (56.5 million US dollars at the current exchange rate) for 2026. Speaking on Saturday at the Assembly of the Republic, the country’s parliament, during the presentation of proposal for a targeted revision of the 2026 Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE), the executive branch plans to boost public investment by 3.6 billion meticais, with priority given to the restoration of infrastructure damaged by floods. According to Levi, the revision stems from the identification of a carry-over balance exceeding 3.5 billion meticais, derived from the budgetary allocation of revenues from Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), which is currently held in the transitional account of Mozambique’s Sovereign Wealth Fund. “The proposal does not alter the strategic objectives of the 2026 Economic and Social Plan and State Budget.

items.title: A bad omen? Syria bans women from university courses
items.summary: The recent announcement that Syrian tertiary institutes will not allow women into some courses has triggered debate. Critics worry it may be a sign that the new Syrian government is restricting women's rights Recent changes to university admissions rules in Syria have put a dent in Lin Najab's plans. The 23-year-old from Damascus is one of the few women at her college studying mechatronics engineering "My original plan was to pursue a master's degree," Najab told DW. But earlier in October, new rules were announced by Syria's education ministry regarding two newly created colleges, the National University of Defense Sciences and the Syrian University for Security Sciences. The former now restricts certain courses exclusively to male students, and the latter almost all of them These new policies could derail Najab's plans. "Now I have to start thinking about other options," she explained.

items.title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
items.summary: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy" Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours.

items.title: UN sounds the alarm over Israel's West Bank military operation
items.summary: The UN has sounded the alarm on Israeli action in the West Bank city of Hebron after hundreds of families were displaced at the weekend. Israel has ordered the military to demolish homes after soldiers were killed there The Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron was met with sharp criticism from the head of the UN as well as the UN's human rights commissioner in comments made on Monday The criticism comes after an Israeli military operation was launched in the occupied West Bank in response to a shootout on Friday that left two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen dead. Three more Israeli soldiers were also injured Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to demolish buildings in the West Bank city of Hebron and to close off the West Bank.

items.title: Fishermen escape from terrorists’ captivity
items.summary: Maputo, 26 Oct (AIM) – A group of three fishermen escaped from captivity at the hands of terrorists last Wednesday after the vessel they were on was hijacked in Mocímboa da Praia district, northern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado. According to local sources, quoted by the independent newsheet “Carta de Moçambique”, the men who escaped from the terrorists were part of a group of 20 fishermen abducted shortly before a military clash that resulted in the deaths of at least three terrorists, who were killed by the Mozambican Navy. Sources added that the fishermen were held captive in the vicinity of the Messalo River. The three individuals who escaped have since returned to their families in the Milamba neighborhood, on the outskirts of the town of Mocímboa da Praia. According to the latest report carried out by the independent conflict registration project ACLED (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project), the terrorists have been increasingly tightening security measures in Mocimboa da Praia, constraining commercial and humanitarian activity.

items.title: 'I cannot teach you integrity': How employee theft is hurting small businesses in Africa
items.summary: Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina shut her waxing studio due to employee theft When popular Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina took a two-week holiday to Europe, she expected to relax. A week into the trip, an Instagram direct message exposed a problem that would ultimately lead to the closure of her business "I was at your studio, I liked everything. The only problem was that I was asked to send money to a different number. It wasn't the number on the wall," a customer wrote to her Boina had opened Waxaholic Studio, a waxing and hydrafacial parlour in Nairobi's central business district, on 1 September 2024. A year later, she had hired a receptionist and two specialists and felt confident enough to take a two-week holiday, her first international trip of the year "I trusted them. It's two rooms and a reception - how do you mess that up?" she recalls thinking "It never occurred to me that maybe I was getting clients and someone else was stealing from me," she tells the BBC The discovery prompted Boina to examine the business more closely.

items.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection The first confirmed Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe International Airport, according to African health officials, as new information from Switzerland contradicts Uganda's account of the Nigerian patient's travel history Uganda , a country reporting no active Ebola infections, has become a focus of investigations into cases thousands of kilometers apart Uganda insists that it has no confirmed active cases of the deadly virus .
